subject: FintechCo - Multi-region perf follow-up & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechco.com>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@fintechco.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Mar 2026 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: FintechCo - Multi-region perf follow-up & next steps

Hi Alex / Priya,

Thanks again for the intro call this morning — great to learn more about FintechCo's EU rollout and the latency/SLA goals you're targeting. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we all have the same plan: 

Call recap (high level):
- Goal: reliable sub-100ms median tail latency for interactive flows in EU region, predictable throughput for peak batch jobs, and clear data residency for EU customers.
- Primary comparisons you mentioned: hyperscaler managed endpoints (AWS/GCP) and a few inference API vendors.
- Constraints: must host EU customer data in-region, security questionnaire in progress, procurement timeline aligned with POC by end of Q2.

How Redwood differentiates (short):
- Predictable latency: Dedicated EU capacity with RBC (reserved burst) and continuous KV caching to reduce cold-starts and tail latency vs shared hyperscaler endpoints.
- Cost controls: batching + quantization recommendations we can tune per workload to beat hyperscaler unit costs without regressing output quality.
- Data residency + auditability: Private deployment options + KMS integrations and per-request logging for audit trails.

Requested validation tests (proposed POC experiments):
1) Geo latency matrix: 50/200/500 concurrent interactive requests from EU-West and US-East; measure p50/p95/p99 and cold vs warm.
2) Throughput burst: 1k concurrent in-region token streams (to validate autoscale/burst behavior).
3) Data residency check: end-to-end proof of EU-only ingress/storage for test dataset and sample audit log.
4) Model parity/quality: run 10 canonical prompts and compare outputs against your hyperscaler baseline for quality/regression.

What we will provide:
- Short-lived test endpoints in eu-west-1 + eu-west-2 (dedicated test pool) and test API keys.
- A perf matrix PDF and mutual action plan (attached).
- Suggested evaluation templates and the scoring sheet for quality/latency comparisons.

Next steps / ask from FintechCo:
- Can you share your target payload sizes and a representative prompt set (10–20 prompts) we can use for parity testing?
- Confirm whether you need physical on-prem data controls or if EU-region cloud isolation (VPC + KMS) is sufficient.
- Preferred dates for POC (we propose starting tests week of 2026-03-29).

I'll loop Jordan and Laura on internal tasks but please reply with the prompt set and any additional constraints. We'll aim to hand you test endpoints by 2026-03-25.

Thanks,
Marissa
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments:
- redwood_perf_matrix_q1_2026.pdf (performance matrix & test plan)
- mutual_action_plan_FIN-2026-001.xlsx (proposed timeline and owners)
From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya.singh@fintechco.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Mar 2026 15:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: FintechCo - Multi-region perf follow-up & next steps

Thanks Marissa — really helpful summary.

We can share a small prompt set (I'll attach a CSV by EOD Monday) and our baseline numbers for AWS Bedrock/GCP Vertex (p95 latency and cost per 1k tokens). A couple quick Qs:
- Will the eu-west endpoints support the quantized model variants you mentioned? We want to test 8-bit/4-bit configs to understand latency/cost tradeoffs.
- Do you have a 24-hour rolling SLA for tail latency you can commit to during POC (so we can validate SLOs under load)?

Preferred POC start week of 03/29 works for us.

Alex
Head of Platform Engineering | FintechCo
alex.johnson@fintechco.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Mar 2026 16:00:00 -07:00
Subject: INTERNAL: FintechCo POC asks + next moves (EU latency + data residency)

Internal notes / ask:
- FintechCo is a strong fit if we can deliver dedicated EU capacity with clear data residency and demonstrate lower p95/p99 vs their hyperscaler baselines.
- They explicitly asked about quantized variants in-region — Jordan, can we support 8-bit and 4-bit variants in the dedicated test pool? If so, what's the expected latency delta p95 vs full precision?
- Laura, please prioritize the security artifacts: SOC2 evidence + KMS integration doc + sample audit logs. They want to see EU-only storage proof.

Action items: 
1) Jordan: provision dedicated eu-west test pool and create two endpoints (quantized-8bit, quantized-4bit) + single full-precision endpoint. Provide test API keys and region-restricted tokens by 2026-03-25.
2) Laura: gather SOC2 attestation excerpt, KMS integration guide, and a sample audit log export for EU-residency proof by 2026-03-24.
3) Marissa: schedule a 60-min POC kickoff for 2026-03-30 and prepare the scoring sheet for latency and quality.

Quoted from Alex's note for context:
> We want to test 8-bit/4-bit configs to understand latency/cost tradeoffs.

I'll keep the FintechCo thread warm and confirm the start date once Jordan confirms endpoints.

-Marissa
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Mar 2026 09:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: INTERNAL: FintechCo POC asks + next moves (EU latency + data residency)

Thanks Marissa — on it.

Plan: I'll provision a dedicated eu-west-1 test pool with three endpoints (full-precision, 8-bit, 4-bit) and reserve a small burst capacity so we can reproduce tail latency under load. Expect endpoints + short-lived test API keys by 2026-03-25 (I'll post the details to the shared Drive link).

Preliminary estimates: quantized 8-bit should improve throughput and reduce p95 by ~15–25% depending on prompt length; 4-bit can give greater cost reduction but may impact output quality for some prompts — we'll surface the quality delta in the parity tests.

I'll coordinate with infra-ops for KMS key scoping to eu-west-1 and confirm audit log extraction steps for Laura.

-Jordan
Senior Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com
